query: My push to the shared branch was rejected. I had amended my last commit. Then I ran `git fetch` because I wanted to see what was on the remote, and after that `git push --force-with-lease` went through with no complaint. Colleagues are saying their work vanished. repo-state.txt is the state I had, gitconfig-fragment.ini is my global config. Explain what happened and give me the setup so it cannot happen again. The repository is not checked out here; work from the files and tell me the commands you would run.
expected_behavior: States the mechanism exactly: --force-with-lease compares the remote's ref against the local remote-tracking ref (refs/remotes/origin/<branch>), so any `git fetch` — even an informational one — refreshes that ref to the colleague's commit and the lease then passes while the colleague's commit is still absent from the pushed history; the earlier 'stale info' rejection was the lease doing its job

Prescribes `--force-if-includes` (git 2.30+) as the actual fix, explaining that it additionally requires the pushed history to contain the remote-tracking tip, or else a pinned `--force-with-lease=<ref>:<expected-sha>` captured before the fetch

Says the lost commits are recoverable from the remote-side or a colleague's reflog / `git fsck` rather than treating the force-push as unrecoverable, and gives the recovery as the first step before any config change

Flags `fp = push --force` and `sync = !git fetch origin && git reset --hard origin/main` in the alias block as the dangerous items — plain --force has no lease at all and the reset --hard alias discards uncommitted work with no reflog entry for it
Names `git range-diff <upstream> <old-tip> <new-tip>` (or an equivalent old-vs-new comparison) as the check that a rewrite dropped nothing, rather than eyeballing `git log`
Notes that `commit.gpgsign = true` plus a rewrite means every rewritten commit is re-signed by whoever ran the rewrite, and that a rebase without signing configured leaves the commits unsigned
Does not recommend plain `git push --force` anywhere, and does not claim `--force-with-lease` alone is sufficient protection

query: I'm mid-merge and stuck. rates.ts.conflicted is the conflicted file, merge-state.txt is the git output, gitconfig-fragment.ini is my global config. Walk me through resolving this properly. Also: on the last conflict I hit, `git status` said the file was unmerged but there were no conflict markers in it at all, which I don't understand. Repository is not checked out here — say what you would run.
expected_behavior: Explains the markerless-but-unmerged file as rerere: `rerere.enabled = true` replayed a previously recorded resolution into the worktree, and with `rerere.autoupdate = true` it is staged as well, so `git commit` would seal a resolution nobody reviewed — and says to inspect `git rerere diff` / the staged content before committing
Says `git rerere forget <path>` clears the recorded resolution but does not put the markers back, and that `git checkout --merge <path>` (or `git checkout -m <path>`) is what regenerates the conflict

Identifies that `merge.conflictstyle = merge` is a two-way presentation that hides the merge base, and prescribes `zdiff3` (git 2.35+) — or reading stage 1 with `git show :1:rates.ts` / `git ls-files -u` — so the original text is visible

Reads the intent of both sides from history before editing (`git log -p <merge-base>..HEAD -- rates.ts` and the same against MERGE_HEAD, using MERGE_HEAD/REBASE_HEAD/CHERRY_PICK_HEAD as appropriate) rather than resolving from the hunk text alone

Composes both changes — TTL-aware cache read plus the three-attempt provider retry — instead of choosing a side, and explicitly rejects `-X ours` / `-X theirs` / `git checkout --ours` as silent deletion
Notes that ours/theirs invert during a rebase or cherry-pick (ours is the upstream being replayed onto, theirs is your own commit), so the labels cannot be read the same way in both operations

Warns that `rebase.autoStash = true` can finish the rebase successfully and still leave the autostash application conflicted, with the entry still in `git stash list`, so a green 'Successfully rebased' line is not proof of a clean tree
Ends by running the project's own checks before committing the merge, and points out that a syntactically clean resolution can still satisfy both branches and pass neither's tests

query: Tidy up my branch before it gets merged. branch-history.txt is the commit list. One of those commits added deploy/creds.env with real tokens and it needs to be gone from history. Separately, yesterday I ran `git reset --hard` and lost a commit I need back, and I already ran `git gc --prune=now` since then. The repository is not checked out here — give me the commands.
expected_behavior: Recovers the lost commit from the reflog and states why it is still there: `git gc --prune=now` does not delete objects a reflog entry still references, so `git reflog` / `git reflog show <branch>` remains the route and only `git reflog expire --expire-unreachable=now --all` followed by `gc --prune=now` actually destroys them

Adds the fallback for a commit no reflog covers (a dropped stash, or a branch deleted with `git branch -D`, which removes that branch's own reflog while HEAD's reflog keeps the entry): `git fsck --unreachable --no-reflogs`, then `git branch <name> <sha>` to re-anchor it
States plainly that the credentials in deploy/creds.env must be rotated regardless of the rewrite, because the commit has already been pushed to origin/feat/refund-window

Names git-filter-repo as the tool for the removal and, if filter-branch is used instead, requires the full cleanup — delete `refs/original/*`, expire all reflogs, then `gc --prune=now` — because the old blob stays readable until every one of those is done

Says rewriting `feat/refund-window` is safe only because it is a topic branch, and that everyone else with it checked out must reset to the new tip rather than merge or pull; a rewrite of `main` is off the table

Uses `git rebase --autosquash` to fold `fixup! feat(refunds): withinWindow helper` into its target, and notes `rebase.autosquash` is off by default so the flag (or config) is required — a plain rebase leaves the fixup commit standing
Deals with the merge commit 54cb85e in the range — either rebase onto the updated main instead of keeping the sync merge, or preserve it with `--rebase-merges` — rather than silently flattening it

Notes that rewriting resets every committer date to now and every SHA while preserving author dates, and that `git range-diff` against the pre-rewrite tip is how the cleanup is verified to have dropped no work

query: I want to run three agents in parallel on this repo, one per task, using worktrees, and then delete the branches that have already landed. repo-state.txt is the current state. Set out the plan and the exact commands. Not checked out here.
expected_behavior: Warns that `refs/stash` is shared across every worktree of a repository, so parallel agents running `git stash` will pop each other's entries — and that per-worktree state is limited to HEAD, the index, the working tree, the in-progress merge/rebase/bisect state and that worktree's reflog

States that a branch can be checked out in only one worktree at a time and that a second `git worktree add` on it fails, so each agent needs its own branch created with `git worktree add <path> -b <branch>`
Notes that untracked and ignored files do not come along — a new worktree has no .env, no node_modules, no build cache — so each worktree needs its own setup step before tests mean anything

Says removal must go through `git worktree remove`, that `rm -rf` of the directory leaves the branch locked ('cannot delete branch ... used by worktree at ...') and the admin directory behind until `git worktree prune`, and that a refused removal means files exist nowhere else so --force is the user's call and not the agent's

Identifies from `git branch --merged main` / `--no-merged main` that feat/currency was squash-merged and therefore reports as unmerged, and uses `git cherry -v main feat/currency` (patch-id comparison) or an equivalent check rather than `git branch -d`'s merged test to decide it has landed
Does not propose `git branch -D` on feat/refund-window: the graph shows it 4 commits ahead of its upstream, so it has not landed
Notes that the worktree's own reflog is deleted along with its admin directory, so deleting the branch after the worktree is gone leaves no local recovery path

query: The CI check on my pull request is failing and I can't tell why. Can you help me see the failure and get the PR merged?
expected_behavior: Does not read skills/git-workflow/SKILL.md
Treats this as GitHub pull-request and Actions work — reading the run logs, the checks and the PR — rather than local branch, worktree or history-rewrite mechanics
Does not open with conflict-style, rerere, reflog or force-with-lease guidance
